articles.title: Agility Robotics partners with FORT to strengthen safety systems for Digit 5
articles.summary: Agility Robotics and FORT Robotics expanded a multi-year relationship into a strategic partnership to strengthen the safety architecture for Digit 5, Agility’s next-generation humanoid robot. articles.title: DeepSeek Harness v0.2 Brings Official Desktop Apps to Its Open-Source Agent Harness
articles.summary: DeepSeek released official macOS and Windows desktop apps for DeepSeek Harness v0.2, an MIT-licensed open-source agent harness that can turn models into agents capable of file work, command execution, planning, document tasks, code review, and scheduled automation. The preview emphasizes extensibility through a plugin-based architecture and supports non-DeepSeek models via OpenAI-compatible endpoints, though DeepSeek warns that breaking changes are likely.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a concrete example of agentic AI tools moving from command-line developer workflows toward broader desktop-based productivity and automation use cases. While still a developer preview, DeepSeek Harness highlights competitive pressure in AI agent platforms and the growing importance of extensible ecosystems, model interoperability, and workflow automation as potential drivers of enterprise AI adoption.

articles.title: The physical AI race will be won in the patent office
articles.summary: The article argues that robotics and physical AI startups may gain durable advantage less from the robot itself and more from patents covering the behavior, mechanisms, models, calibration methods, or system interactions that make the robot valuable. It emphasizes that startups should protect one or two core “crown jewel” inventions early, while selectively using trade secrets for processes that are hard to reverse-engineer.
articles.advisor_relevance: This matters because physical AI may create value through proprietary behavior, motion systems, and control architectures rather than only hardware unit sales. For investors, the article highlights IP ownership, litigation exposure, and defensible patent portfolios as important diligence factors for robotics startups and potential acquirers as the sector matures.
